The realm is LegionCore 7.3.5 and its databases: a download of %1$s, then about 2 GB on the phone (%2$s free).

The client is 42.3 GB, from its host over HTTP. The app checks every file against the zip\'s own checksums and takes the stock Wow-64.exe out of the client\'s storage, where the build lists its hash. Allow about 50 GB free (%1$s now). A dropped connection carries on where it stopped.
What is downloaded is kept: stop it and press it again, or close the app, and it carries on.
Add my client from a folder
Add my client from a zip
The realm needs maps, vmaps and DB2 tables made from the client with LegionCore\'s own tools. It takes a while on a phone (the maps, then the vmaps), with the app kept running in the background.
Set up the client for the realm
Legion\'s login is a Battle.net one: the account is an e-mail address and a password, kept on this phone.
Add server data made on a computer (zip)
Creatures walk around obstacles with it. It takes hours on a phone; without it they walk straight lines.
Starts the realm on this phone, then the game, which signs in by itself. The first start of the realm takes longer: it loads and updates its databases.
The first start takes several minutes: the realm loads and updates its databases.

Off: only this phone connects. Applies at the next start of the realm.

Downloads, the realm and the game keep running while you use another app or the screen is off, if Android lets the app run in the background.

Only the client\'s build record and its storage are kept; its Wow-64.exe is always the stock one from that storage (a different one is kept beside, named .not-stock). Its server data and set-up copy are made on the phone.

Accounts and characters, as SQL. The app makes one before it updates the realm or resets its databases.

This removes the realm, its databases (accounts and characters), the client and the server data: %1$s. The other games are not touched. Back up first if you want to keep your characters somewhere else.
